issues.detail: The Greek 'εις παντας' (eis pantas) means 'to all' or 'towards all,' but the Vietnamese translation 'đến với mọi người' (reached everyone/came to everyone) changes the sense of obedience being directed toward everyone, rather than the obedience of the people reaching its fulfillment.

The Greek 'ακεραιους' (akeraious) means 'blameless', 'irreproachable', or 'sincere'. The Vietnamese translation 'tinh sạch' (pure/clean) is a common theological rendering, but the primary issue is the structure of 'σοφους μεν... ακεραιους δε' which implies a contrast in quality (wise vs. blameless), which the Vietnamese captures well, but the first clause remains the primary fidelity issue.
